chapters.1.lds: Doctrine and Covenants 27:13 also speaks of the fulness of times (verse 10). Why does the opening blessing lead into a prayer for understanding?
chapters.1.summary: The letter opens in Paul’s name to the saints at Ephesus. It blesses God for choosing them in Christ before the world’s foundation. In Christ they have redemption through his blood and forgiveness. God plans to sum up all things in Christ. They were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, a pledge of their inheritance. Paul has heard of their faith and love and gives thanks. He prays that they will know their hope and God’s power. That power raised Christ and made him head over all things.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson applies the building image to Christ, apostles, and prophets. How do good works follow received grace rather than supply a reason to boast?
chapters.2.summary: Paul says the readers were dead in trespasses and followed this world’s course. God, rich in mercy, made them alive with Christ. They are saved by grace through faith, so no one can boast. They are created for good works. As Gentiles they were once far from Israel’s covenants and without hope. Christ’s blood brought them near. He broke down the dividing wall and made the two into one new man. Now they are built together into a holy temple.
chapters.3.lds: Why does the speaker ask the hearers not to lose heart over his troubles?
chapters.3.summary: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus for the Gentiles. A mystery was made known to him by revelation. Earlier generations did not know it as it is now revealed. The Gentiles are fellow heirs and members of the same body. Paul, the least of all saints, was given grace to announce Christ’s riches. He asks them not to lose heart over his troubles. He kneels and prays that they be strengthened and rooted in love. He ends with praise to God, who can do far more than they ask.
chapters.4.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches that different responsibilities strengthen and unify the Church. How does truthful speech protect members of the same body?
chapters.4.summary: Paul, a prisoner, urges them to walk worthy of their calling. He names one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, and one God. Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds, and teachers to build up the body. The body is to grow up into Christ, its head. They must no longer walk as the Gentiles do. They are to put off the old man and put on the new. He gives commands about lying, anger, stealing, and speech. They are to forgive each other as God forgave them.
chapters.5.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches family care through the Savior's example. How does Christ's self-giving love shape the command to husbands?
chapters.5.summary: Paul tells them to imitate God and walk in love, as Christ loved them. Sexual immorality, greed, and coarse talk should not be named among them. They were once darkness and are now light in the Lord. They should use the time wisely and be filled with the Spirit. They should sing, give thanks, and submit to one another. Wives are told to submit to their husbands as to the Lord. Husbands are told to love their wives as Christ loved the assembly. Paul quotes Genesis on two becoming one flesh and calls it a great mystery.
chapters.6.lds: The selected lesson teaches care for children and protection through the armor of God. Why does the armor passage lead into prayer for the imprisoned speaker?
chapters.6.summary: Children are told to obey their parents, and fathers not to provoke their children. Servants are told to obey their masters as serving Christ. Masters are told to stop threatening, for they have the same Master in heaven. Paul then tells all to be strong in the Lord. They are to put on the whole armor of God. He names truth as a belt, faith as a shield, and the Spirit’s sword. They are to pray at all times. He asks prayer for himself, an ambassador in chains, and sends Tychicus.
